_comment: Order-layer and rules-based AI parameters. Not engine physics — these govern how orders (MoveOrder, MarkOrder, etc.) and the rules-based AI translate high-level intent into SpeedMode/direction requests. The neural network path bypasses all of these except where it issues orders explicitly.

movement._comment: Brake-to-turn and close-proximity brakes applied in _compute_movement_intent (order layer only — not used by the neural network direct-drive path).
movement._comment_brake_turn: Heading change above this triggers brake-to-turn: the order forces SpeedMode.STANDSTILL so the player decelerates before pivoting. 75=current, 90=original less aggressive.
movement._comment_brake_min: Brake-to-turn and close-prox checks only fire above this ground speed. Below it, turn rate is already high enough to pivot freely without braking.
movement._comment_close_prox: Lateral-overshoot brake: within close_prox_radius_m of target, if velocity cos-sim < threshold, force STANDSTILL. Prevents a player arriving at pace from the wrong angle blowing past and orbiting. cos 0.3 = ~73° off-axis.
movement._comment_sprint_to_ball: Rules-AI sprint decision: sprint if opponent_sprint_ETA * margin < self_jog_ETA. <1.0 = aggressive (sprint even when comfortably ahead); 1.0 = sprint only when opponent wins the exact race; >1.0 = conservative (only sprint when clearly losing — opponent must be that much faster).
movement._comment_intercept_overshoot: Loose-ball intercept margin: player aims this fraction of their distance-to-intercept past the intercept point, in the direction of ball travel. 0.0 = run exactly to the intercept (player and ball arrive simultaneously); 0.15 = player aims 15% further so they arrive before the ball and have time to set their feet. Only applied when the ball is moving (velocity > 0.1 m/s).

repulsion._comment: Player-repulsion steering — used ONLY in steering.py / MoveOrder handling. NOT engine physics. radius_m: distance at which repulsion begins. strength_base: peak directional weight at d=0 (m/s-equivalent, blended into heading not force). ball_carrier_repulsion_mult: extra boost when the moving player has the ball. ball_carrier_speed_penalty_max: max fractional speed penalty for ball carriers (0.45 = 45% reduction). speed_penalty_scale: converts |net_repulsion| to speed penalty fraction. alignment_dot_threshold: trigger orthogonal nudge when rel_vel . net_repulsion < this (i.e. heading nearly straight into obstacle). min_orthogonal_adjust_mps: sideways nudge magnitude (primary tuning knob). max_deflection_deg: hard cap on total direction deflection from repulsion.
repulsion._comment_gate: Ahead/behind gate: an obstacle is ignored as 'not in the way' if its position (predicted velocity_lookahead_s seconds ahead) projects behind the player along their direction of travel, beyond behind_tolerance_m of slack. behind_tolerance_m: how far behind the player an obstacle can be before it's ignored regardless of straight-line distance. velocity_lookahead_s: how far ahead (seconds) to predict the obstacle's position using its current velocity before running the ahead/behind test -- an obstacle moving away from the player's path drifts further behind (more likely gated out); one converging into the path drifts further ahead (stays gated in) even if currently borderline. 0.0 = ignore velocity, use current position only.
repulsion._comment_boundary: Boundary repulsion (ball carriers only): steers a carry path away from the pitch edge before it's crossed, using the SAME blend/speed-penalty machinery as player repulsion above (added into net_rep, so max_deflection_deg/ball_carrier_speed_penalty_max still cap it). Closes a real gap: engine/match.py's boundary_braking_params only ever applies while chasing a LOOSE ball -- once a player actually has the ball, movement runs through this function instead, which previously had zero boundary awareness (confirmed: a real traced episode picked up the ball 2m from the corner and sprinted dead straight through the touchline a second later). boundary_radius_m: distance from the pitch edge at which this starts (0.0 disables it entirely -- pre-existing tests/callers that don't pass a `pitch` get skipped regardless). boundary_strength_base: peak weight at the line itself (d=0), same units/scale as strength_base above -- picked to land in the same ballpark as the EFFECTIVE player-carrier repulsion strength (strength_base * ball_carrier_repulsion_mult = 1.5 at contact), not yet empirically tuned against real carry-near-boundary episodes the way the player-repulsion values above have been -- treat as a starting point.

shot_selection._comment: Smart shot placement — used ONLY by shot_selection.py (an AI-layer decision, not engine physics). corner_tolerance_m: inset from each post (aim point y = ±(goal_width/2 - this)) so shots don't literally target the frame edge. height_tolerance_frac: random shot height is drawn uniformly from [0, this * goal_height_m] -- same height used for both corner candidates so the corner choice isn't confounded by height. The corner itself is NOT random: chosen by comparing ball flight time (real ballistic solve) against the goalkeeper's accel-aware ETA (same sprint_eta model orders.py's GK sprint-vs-jog decision uses), evaluated at the goalkeeping.py interception plane (goal_frame_margin_m in front of the true goal line) so this matches what a real save attempt does.

marking._comment: MarkOrder AI behaviour: marker stands between a target opposition player and the ball, and switches to GetPossession-style chase/tackle when the target has the ball or the ball comes within mark_intercept_radius_m. mark_standoff_m: distance from the target (toward the ball) the marker tries to hold.

boundary_braking._comment: Match._run_get_possession_behaviour's loose-ball chase (shared by GetPossessionOrder and MarkOrder's intercept fallback): when closing on a ball near the pitch boundary, caps arrival speed via v^2=2*a*d kinematics so the player can stop before carrying it out themselves, UNLESS the player's own team touched the ball last (Ball.last_touched_by_player_id) -- in that case braking is skipped entirely (sprint blindly), since the reward model's untouched-exit floor ('invalid', 0 reward) is already gone for us either way once our own team has touched it, so caution there can only cost a recovery, never avoid a worse outcome. See own_team_touched_last in that method for the full reasoning.
boundary_braking._comment_brake_buffer: Extra fixed buffer beyond pickup_radius_m subtracted from the raw distance-to-boundary before computing the safe arrival speed. Corrects for discretisation slack (speed mode is only re-evaluated once per tick, so a player can travel a bit further than the ideal continuous-braking stopping distance before the slower mode actually takes effect) -- not a physically-derived quantity, tuned empirically (see test_ball_out_overrun.py).
boundary_braking._comment_abandon_margin: Only applies when the player's own team did NOT touch the ball last (see _comment above -- that case always goes for it regardless of risk). If the RAW (pre-clamp) boundary margin at the projected intercept point is <= this value, the chase is abandoned entirely (player holds position) instead of continuing to close in at the computed near-zero safe speed -- letting the ball roll out untouched scores 'invalid' (0 reward) instead of a penalised 'ball_out' (-4). CAUTION when tuning this up toward 0.0: raw_margin is already negative (pickup_radius_m + brake_buffer_m subtracted off) in perfectly recoverable cases -- test_ball_out_overrun.py's validated 0.5m-inside-the-line pickup sits at raw_margin=-0.65 and DOES recover cleanly (no overrun, real possession gained) despite that, which is why the default here is -1.0, not 0.0 (0.0 was tried first and broke that exact test -- it abandoned a recoverable chase). A real FAILING episode traced this session (0.54m overrun despite the safe-speed cap already being 0) had raw_margin=-0.91, uncomfortably close to that same recoverable case's -0.65 -- raw distance-to-boundary alone doesn't cleanly separate recoverable from doomed chases; the ball's own sustained drift speed toward the boundary looked like the more likely real discriminator (the failing case drifted ~0.7m/s over 3s, the recoverable test case crawls at 0.05m/s) but that signal isn't wired in here yet. Treat this default as conservative-by-necessity, not fully tuned -- raise it carefully, re-running test_ball_out_overrun.py plus real worst-episode traces after each change, not on a single data point.

interception._comment: engine.interception.intercept_target's deceleration-aware solve (Match._run_get_possession_behaviour's loose-ball chase only -- a chased CARRIER doesn't decelerate the same way, so that call site never passes this). The base (decel=0) constant-velocity solve assumes the ball holds its CURRENT speed for the whole chase, which is never physically true, and has a real, confirmed failure mode beyond just directional bias: a numerical singularity whenever the ball's speed crosses the chaser's own top speed, which can produce a predicted intercept point hundreds of metres off the pitch for a real multi-tick window (confirmed on a real traced 'invalid' episode -- the chaser aimed at that nonsense point instead of anywhere near the actual ball, and missed the ball by 1.89m as a direct result; confirmed fixed by enabling this -- same seed, chaser gets genuine possession instead).
interception._comment_assumed_ball_decel: Defaults to the ball's own real configured ground-friction deceleration (physics.json: ball_physics.rolling_friction_coefficient [0.05] * world.gravity_mps2 [9.81] = 0.4905 m/s^2), kept as its own independently-tunable value here rather than reading physics.json directly -- the solve only needs a reasonable ESTIMATE of how fast the ball is slowing (a kicked ball spends part of its flight airborne, where drag behaves differently from rolling friction), so this can be retuned for the solve's own behaviour without touching real ball physics, or vice versa. 0.0 disables the deceleration-aware solve entirely, reproducing the exact prior (constant-velocity-only) behaviour.

push_kick._comment: MoveOrder / GetPossessionOrder push-kick: when push_kick_enabled=True the ball carrier kicks the ball flat (no ballistic loft -- straight toward the order's target_position, via Player.kick_with_direction) rather than dribbling, then sprints to it. Only fires when the remaining distance to target_position exceeds min_dist_m (so the player doesn't kick near the destination -- this is also what stops repeated touches overshooting target_position, since there's no separate travel-distance cap on the kick itself; how far it actually rolls is real ground physics driven by speed_factor, not a config distance). Opponents whose ETA to target_position is less than the carrier's ETA x clearance_margin are considered a threat — the kick is skipped if any such opponent exists.
push_kick._comment_min_dist: Don't push-kick when this close to the destination.
push_kick._comment_speed_factor: Ball is kicked at speed_factor x carrier's free-sprint speed, ensuring it stays ahead of the running player.
push_kick._comment_clearance: ETA safety margin: if any opponent's ETA to landing spot < carrier's ETA x clearance_margin, skip the kick. 0.95 = 5% margin.
push_kick._comment_heading: Don't push-kick if the player's current heading differs from the kick direction by more than this many degrees. Prevents kicking sideways or backwards.
